d: THE HETERONYM COLLIDES WITH ESL PEDAGOGY, AND THE CARDS ARE HASHTAGS. An Instagram English-teaching caption with twenty hashtags and an eight-minute YouTube grammar explainer, on a query about the Dodecad.
reading:
THE LINGUISTIC SENSE WINS THE CARD STRIP. «heteronym dodecad» was one of the two captures I logged as NOT FOUND before the export recovery, and reading it now shows why it matters: the composed answer DOES give the Dodecad — "the specific twelve-part Dodecad authorial/heteronym system used in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive project" — but the visible card strip is ESL pedagogy. Tear and tear, wind and wind, with #learnenglish #ieltstips #english10minutesaday.

Three senses contest the query: the linguistic heteronym (same spelling, different pronunciation), the literary heteronym (Pessoa), and DODECAD K12b — a genetic-ancestry calculator using twelve reference populations, which the answer also names. Both halves of the query have prior occupants in unrelated fields, and the tail of the strip belongs to the grammar lesson.

The archive is present in the answer and absent from the visible cards — which is the arrangement MANUS named on 28 July as "the reverse of compositional bystanding", here inverted again: present in composition, absent from the strip.
analysis: As screenshotted: single-referent adoption — *the consolidated registry of twelve distinct authorial pseudonyms or heteronyms (the Dodecad) within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive system... a multi-voiced literary and architectural project where different persona-authors manage distinct theoretical, poetic, and systemic outputs* — with the Zenodo Provenance Registry v1.1 first organic and leesharks.com behind it. As transcribed after regeneration: the answer splits three ways — linguistic heteronyms (lead/lead, tear/tear), *the specific twelve-part “Dodecad” authorial/heteronym system used in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive project*, and the Dodecad K12b/K12a admixture calculators — with ESL Instagram captions and pronunciation explainers entering the source set. Both co-tenants are real lexical neighbors; the finding is the boundary’s instability: within one session the same query renders as proper-noun resolution and as common-noun disambiguation. The 19 June GitHub issue (*Account blocked and 850+ records removed*, carrying the Attribution Severance finding — 941 DOIs invisible to DataCite) surfaces inside the regenerated source set: the termination record is now part of the term’s retrieval neighborhood. Zenodo v1.1 records serve as SERP sources in both compositions; live-resolution status is a follow-up check.
